verdict.rationale: Granola documents an official MCP server that connects Claude, ChatGPT and other AI tools to meeting notes, with search across notes and transcripts. The docs say nothing about the authentication method, and action-item retrieval is only described for the REST API, not for MCP. There is also no hands-on or community confirmation that the MCP connection works. Missing for 10: documented OAuth authentication for the MCP server, explicit action-item querying via MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an official MCP server lets Claude or any MCP client query my meetings — search, transcripts, action items — with OAuth, no glue code

citations.quote: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI tools to your Granola meeting notes via MCP. Query your notes, search transcripts, and get meeting insights in your favorite AI assistants.
Once connected you can use this to: search through your meeting notes, find specific topics discussed in past meetings
